prompt:
Create ONE high-resolution comparison board containing THREE COMPLETE DESKTOP WEB APPLICATION SCREEN MOCKUPS, stacked vertically, equal size, each roughly 1440x820 landscape. This is a UI design comparison, not a poster. Label the three mockups A, B, C in a small gutter outside the UI. App name Ride Archive. A private local dashcam trip video browser. Use provided real road footage reference inside ALL video players and filmstrip thumbnails; preserve this actual road scene, do not invent prettier landscape footage. Render the content exactly as a functional polished app, crisp typography, real buttons, no imaginary charts, GPS map, speed readings or invented telemetry.
Every screen MUST have the user's pinned composition: compact left day/session rail 220px wide, very large 16:9 video player on the right using the reference road frame, bottom thumbnail filmstrip, compact player toolbar, and unobtrusive top app bar. Main player takes at least two thirds of the content width. Header: Ride Archive, a small local-files indicator, trip dropdown video_full_ride, search, Import folder button. Day rail: Trip timeline, 9 recording days, Jan 01 2025 selected with 284 clips, Jan 02 2025 343 clips, Aug 18 2026 21 clips, Aug 26 2026 155 clips, Aug 27 2026 263 clips, Sep 01 2026 19 clips, Sep 02 2026 22 clips, Sep 03 2026 4 clips, Nov 06 2026 22 clips. Show selected day expanded with a few session rows using neutral Session 01, Session 02, Session 03 labels, not invented places. Main title January 01, 2025 with subdued Camera date below, segmented Day / Entire trip control. Under the video play icon, previous/next, -10s/+10s, cumulative scrubber, 1x, volume, fullscreen. Under toolbar horizontally arranged 6 road thumbnail cells with filename times and clear active amber edge. Small bookmark icon and Import health button 20 issues; footer Videos stay on this device. No stats that weren't supplied.
A — expedition instrument console: near-black graphite #151816, dark olive charcoal rail #1b201c, warm off-white #e5e9df text, muted sage #9aa597 secondary text, muted amber #e9b76d selected indicators. Flat restrained surfaces, thin subtle borders, sans grotesk title, monospace small camera time labels. Main video flush with its player frame. Luxurious precision, calm, exact alignment. Clear amber import button. Strong but quiet active day block. Most immersive. No gradients or ornamental gauges.
B — same expedition-console design language interpreted as a daylight archive: warm off-white #f2f1e9 app background, pale sage #e3e7dc rail, dark forest #253c31 headings, deep forest player toolbar and amber scrubber. Same typography, same spatial structure and real data; frame footage with a slim dark surround. Slightly more breathing room, exceptionally readable day rows and editorial day heading. Functional quiet filing-system quality, no paper texture or stickers.
C — same console design language as compact screening view: neutral charcoal #202220 app, slim pale top header, rail with hairline day dividers and tiny amber selection marker, bigger footage relative to all other elements, title in a single compact strip, player tools in one efficient row. Filmstrip occupies the full width of main region. Amber reserved for current position. More utilitarian density while retaining generous touch targets and readable text. No ornamental widgets.
Render all THREE complete desktop screens, same resolution and care, not cropped and no overlapping. No device mockup or external scenery. Comparison board aspect ratio approximately 1:2 vertical. The subject is the real road footage in the actual useful UI.
